# The core library

<!-- covers: LR 15 -->
*Agent mode. Human mode: [The core library](../guide/library.md). Generated by `conformance/tools/libref.py` from the declarations
of `library/fortis` and the effect data of `reference/library/effects`; do not edit.
Source of truth: LR 15 for the inventory, and each declaration's own contract.*

> Preview: the core runtime inventory (LR 15) arrives in v0.4.

Every public declaration of the seven core modules (LR 15): each exported declaration, every member of an
exported interface (whose members share its visibility, LR 4.4) and every variant of an exported enum, with its
signature as the library declares it, the effects it declares and the contract its documentation comment
states. The check counts these against the module sources independently of this page. A `trusted` operation is
implemented by the toolchain, and its comment is its review record (LR 11.3). `fortis.prelude` is imported into
every module; the other modules need an `import` (LR 4.3). What is not listed here does not exist in Language
1.0's core library; the gaps against the Language Reference are recorded as D-58.

The Effects column is `pure` or `noalloc` where the signature claims it, then the effects the operation has,
which a caller inherits (LR 11.1, 11.3): `alloc`, `fail` (a `try` function), `suspend` (`async`), `recovers`,
`block`, `io` (a capability's method, or an operation that takes an authority), `mutate`, `nondet`, and
`writes self` (an impure `editable self` method). `none` is an impure operation with no effect to declare; a
type has none.

## `fortis.prelude`

Imported into every module: the built-in types, the optional and outcome operations, the built-in interfaces (LR 4.3, LR 6.2, LR 6.10).

### `class Int`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | checked 64-bit two's-complement addition; fails `numeric.overflow` outside [-2^63, 2^63-1]; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | checked subtraction; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func mul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | checked multiplication; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1), no allocation |
| `trusted pure try func div(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | truncating division; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0 and `numeric.overflow` for -2^63 / -1; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func rem(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure; fail | remainder with the sign of a; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` when b = 0; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func shiftLeft(a: Int, bits: Int) Int` | pure; fail | a * 2^bits; fails `numeric.shift_range` unless 0 <= bits < 64 and `numeric.overflow` when the result is out of range; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | addition modulo 2^64 into [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | subtraction modulo 2^64; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func wrappingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | multiplication modulo 2^64; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingAdd(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | addition clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingSub(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | subtraction clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func saturatingMul(a: Int, b: Int) Int` | pure | multiplication clamped to [-2^63, 2^63-1]; total; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func validate(value: Int) Int` | pure; fail | the value when it lies in the refinement of the receiver type; fails `refinement.out_of_range` otherwise; O(1) |

Variants: `HalfEven`, `HalfAwayFromZero`, `TowardZero`, `AwayFromZero`.

### `class Decimal`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the sum at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when it needs more than 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` when the integer part does not fit (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the difference at the larger operand scale, rounded half to even when needed; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func mul(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the product at the sum of the scales, rounded half to even above 28 fractional digits or 96 coefficient bits; fails `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure try func div(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the quotient at the largest scale that fits, rounded half to even; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` and `numeric.overflow` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure try func rem(a: Decimal, b: Decimal) Decimal` | pure; fail | the remainder with the sign of the dividend at the larger operand scale; fails `numeric.divide_by_zero` (6.4); O(digits^2) |
| `trusted pure func round(value: Decimal, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal` | pure | value rounded to scale by mode; total; O(digits) |
| `trusted pure try func fromFloat(x: Float, scale: Int<0..28>, mode: RoundingMode) Decimal` | pure; fail | the binary value of x rounded to scale by mode; fails `numeric.overflow` for a non-finite x or an integer part that does not fit (6.4); O(digits) |
| `trusted pure func scale(self) Int<0..28>` | pure | the number of fractional digits; O(1) |

### `class String`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func from(text: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | an owned copy of the view; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `pure func empty() String` | pure | — |
| `trusted pure func scalarCount(self) Int` | pure | the number of Unicode scalar values; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func byteCount(self) Int` | pure | the UTF-8 length in bytes; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func trim(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its leading and trailing Unicode White_Space (U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) scalars; a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trimStart(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its leading White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func trimEnd(self) StringView from self` | pure | the view without its trailing White_Space scalars (as trim); a view of the same text, no allocation; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func find(self, needle: StringView) Int<0..>?` | pure | the scalar offset (the unit of slice and scalarAt) of the first occurrence of needle, null when it does not occur; an empty needle occurs at 0; no allocation; at most O(n * m) in bytes for a text of n bytes and a needle of m |
| `pure func contains(self, needle: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when find(needle) is present: an empty needle is contained in every text |
| `trusted pure func startsWith(self, prefix: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when the text begins with prefix (an empty prefix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a prefix of m |
| `trusted pure func endsWith(self, suffix: StringView) Bool` | pure | true exactly when the text ends with suffix (an empty suffix always does); no allocation; O(m) in bytes for a suffix of m |
| `trusted pure func split(self, separator: StringView) List[String]` | pure; alloc | the pieces between the non-overlapping occurrences of separator, found left to right, as owned strings; a separator at either end gives an empty piece there, a text without the separator gives one piece (itself), and an empty separator occurs nowhere, so it gives one piece; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func lines(self) List[String]` | pure; alloc | the lines of the text as owned strings, each ended by a line feed or by a carriage return and a line feed (neither stays in the line); the text after the last terminator is a line only when it is not empty, so "" has no lines and "a\n" has one; a carriage return not before a line feed stays in the line; allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func replace(self, old: StringView, new: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | a copy of the text with every non-overlapping occurrence of old, found left to right, replaced by new; an empty old occurs nowhere, so the copy is unchanged; allocates; O(n) in bytes plus the find cost |
| `trusted pure func asciiUpper(self) String` | pure; alloc | a copy with the ASCII letters a-z mapped to A-Z and every other scalar unchanged (not Unicode case mapping: that depends on the Unicode version and the language, and changes lengths); allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `trusted pure func asciiLower(self) String` | pure; alloc | a copy with the ASCII letters A-Z mapped to a-z and every other scalar unchanged (as asciiUpper); allocates; O(n) in bytes |
| `pure func repeat(self, times: Int<0..>) String` | pure; alloc | the text written times in a row: "" when times is 0 or the text is empty; allocates; O(times * n) in bytes |
| `pure func join(parts: ListView[String], separator: StringView) String` | pure; alloc | the parts in order with separator between neighbours: "" for no parts and the part itself for one; allocates; O(total length) |

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func days(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 86400 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) (n bounded by the 64-bit count) |
| `trusted pure func hours(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 3600 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func minutes(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 60 * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func seconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 10^9 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func milliseconds(n: Int<0..>) Duration` | pure | n * 10^6 nanoseconds; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func add(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration` | pure; fail | sum of the signed 64-bit nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func sub(a: Duration, b: Duration) Duration` | pure; fail | difference of the nanosecond counts; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func multiply(d: Duration, factor: Int) Duration` | pure; fail | the count times factor; fails `numeric.overflow`; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func nanoseconds(self) Int` | pure | the signed 64-bit nanosecond count; O(1) |

### `class List[T]`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted pure func default() List[T]` | pure | an empty list with no allocation until the first push; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func of(...items: owned T) List[T]` | pure; alloc | a list holding the arguments in order; allocates once; O(n) |
| `trusted pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of elements; O(1) |
| `trusted func push(editable self, item: owned T)` | alloc, writes self | appends item; amortised O(1) (capacity doubles), worst case O(n) for the growth step |
| `trusted func pop(editable self) T?` | writes self | removes and returns the last element, null when empty; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the element at index, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `trusted pure try func at(self, index: Int) T` | pure; fail | the element at index; fails `collection.index` outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `trusted try func set(editable self, index: Int, value: owned T)` | fail, writes self | replaces the element at index, dropping the old value; fails `collection.index`; O(1) |
| `trusted func clear(editable self)` | writes self | removes and drops every element; rejected for a linear element type (10.7): consume them instead; O(n) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | pure | — |
| `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | — |
| `pure func reversed(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | — |
| `pure func concat(self, other: ListView[T]) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | — |
| `pure func countWhere(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Int` | pure | — |
| `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) List[U] where U: linear` | pure; alloc | — |
| `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | — |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every element in order (X-479); the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `try func tryEach(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Outcome[Void])` | fail | as `each`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) List[U]` | pure; alloc, fail | as `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new list dropped (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the callback per element U must be non-linear: failure drops earlier results (10.7, E-OBL-003). (E-OBL-003: LR 5.3) |
| `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A` | pure | step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an element, once per element in order, and returns the next accumulator (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A` | pure; fail | as `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it (X-479); O(n) plus the callback per element |
| `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for some element; stops at the first one that passes (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for every element; stops at the first one that fails (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?` | pure | the index of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable` | pure | whether some element equals target (X-479); O(n) |
| `pure func enumerate(self) List[(Int, T)] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | each element copied with its index, in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func zip[U](self, other: ListView[U]) List[(T, U)] where T implements Copyable, U implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | pairs of copies of the elements at the same index of self and other, as many as the shorter has (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, m)) |
| `pure func take(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the first n elements, all of them when n is at least count(), none when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, count)) |
| `pure func skip(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements after the first n, none when n is at least count(), all when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(count) |
| `pure func flatMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) List[U]) List[U] where U: linear` | pure; alloc | the lists f returns for each element, joined in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) plus the sizes of the lists plus the callback per element |
| `pure func chunked(self, size: Int<1..>) List[List[T]] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements in lists of size elements, the last one shorter when size does not divide count() (X-479); allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func sortedBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) List[T] where T implements Copyable, K implements Comparable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements ordered by key(element), smaller keys first, elements with equal keys in their original order (a stable merge sort over indexes); key is called once per element (X-479); allocates; O(n log n) comparisons plus n callbacks |
| `pure func groupBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) Map[K, List[T]] where T implements Copyable, K implements Copyable, K implements Hashable, K implements Equatable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements gathered by key(element) into a Map from each key to its elements in their original order; the keys are in the order they first appear (X-479); allocates; expected O(n) plus n callbacks |
| `trusted pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | pure | a cursor over read loans of the elements in order; O(1) to create, O(1) per step |
| `trusted func consumeEach(owned self, visit: fn mut(owned T) Void)` | none | consumes the list (10.7): no early exit, so no element is left unvisited; an empty list makes no calls intrinsic: calls visit once per element in order, transferring each element out; O(n) plus the callback per element |

| `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?` | pure | the index of the first element holds is true for, null when none does (X-479); O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable` | pure | whether some element equals target (X-479); O(n) |
| `pure func enumerate(self) List[(Int, T)] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | each element copied with its index, in order (X-479); allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func zip[U](self, other: ListView[U]) List[(T, U)] where T implements Copyable, U implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | pairs of copies of the elements at the same index of self and other, as many as the shorter has (X-479); allocates; O(min(n, m)) |

| `pure func skip(self, n: Int) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements after the first n, none when n is at least count(), all when n is 0 or less (X-479); allocates; O(count) |

| `pure func sortedBy[K](self, key: pure fn(T) K) List[T] where T implements Copyable, K implements Comparable` | pure; alloc | copies of the elements ordered by key(element), smaller keys first, elements with equal keys in their original order (a stable merge sort over indexes); key is called once per element (X-479); allocates; O(n log n) comparisons plus n callbacks |

## `fortis.collections`

Collection algorithms (LR 6.7).

### `class Deque[T] implements Iterable[T, ListCursor[T]]`

`front` holds the items from the front end, the first item last, so popping the front is its `pop`; `back` holds the
rest, the last item last. An end that runs dry takes half of the other end's items over, which costs as many moves as
the pushes that filled that end, so both ends are amortised O(1) and no item is copied.

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `pure func default() Deque[T]` | pure | an empty deque; O(1) |
| `pure func fromList(items: owned List[T]) Deque[T]` | pure | a deque of the items of the list in order, the first at the front, taking the list's storage; O(1) |
| `pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of items; O(1) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | pure | whether the deque holds no item; O(1) |
| `func pushBack(editable self, item: owned T)` | alloc, writes self | adds item after the last one; amortised O(1) |
| `func pushFront(editable self, item: owned T)` | alloc, writes self | adds item before the first one; amortised O(1) |
| `func popFront(editable self) T?` | alloc, writes self | removes and returns the first item, null when empty; amortised O(1), worst case O(count) for the rebalance |
| `func popBack(editable self) T?` | alloc, writes self | removes and returns the last item, null when empty; amortised O(1), worst case O(count) for the rebalance |
| `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the item at index, counted from the front, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `pure func peekFront(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the first item, null when empty; O(1) |
| `pure func peekBack(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the last item, null when empty; O(1) |
| `trusted pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | pure | a cursor over read loans of the items from the front to the back, the items of `front` last to first and then those of `back`; the cursor lists them when it is made, O(count), and each step is O(1) |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every item from the front to the back; the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `try func tryEach(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Outcome[Void])` | fail | as `each`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func map[U](self, f: pure fn(T) U) Deque[U]` | pure; alloc | a deque of the results of f for every item, in order; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure try func tryMap[U](self, f: pure fn(T) Outcome[U]) Deque[U]` | pure; alloc, fail | as `map`, stopping at the first failure of the callback and returning it, with the new deque dropped; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func filter(self, keep: pure fn(T) Bool) Deque[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a deque of copies of the items keep is true for, in order; allocates; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A` | pure | step gets a read loan of the accumulator and an item, once per item from the front to the back, and returns the next accumulator; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure try func tryFold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) Outcome[A]) A` | pure; fail | as `fold`, stopping at the first failure of step and returning it; O(n) plus the callback per item |
| `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for some item; stops at the first one that passes; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for every item; stops at the first one that fails; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the first item holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func indexWhere(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Int?` | pure | the position, counted from the front, of the first item holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func contains(self, target: T) Bool where T implements Equatable` | pure | whether some item equals target; O(n) |
| `pure func toList(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a list of copies of the items from the front to the back; allocates; O(n) |

### `class SortedSet[T] implements Iterable[T, ListCursor[T]]`

`items` holds the members in ascending order, each once, so a lookup is a binary search over `get`, O(log n). Making
room for a member or closing the gap a removal leaves moves the members after it, one pop and one push each, so `add`
and `remove` are O(n) in the members after the one added or removed; the set operations merge two ascending lists in
one pass, O(n + m).

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `pure func default() SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable` | pure | an empty set; O(1) |
| `pure func fromList(items: owned List[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable` | pure; alloc | a set of the items of the list, each once; the list's duplicates are dropped; O(n) times the members each add moves |
| `pure func count(self) Int` | pure | the number of members; O(1) |
| `pure func isEmpty(self) Bool` | pure | whether the set has no member; O(1) |
| `func add(editable self, item: owned T) Bool where T implements Comparable` | alloc, writes self | adds item, true when it was absent; O(log n) to find its place and O(n) in the members after it to make room |
| `pure func contains(self, item: T) Bool where T implements Comparable` | pure | whether item is a member; O(log n) |
| `func remove(editable self, item: T) Bool where T implements Comparable` | alloc, writes self | removes item, true when it was a member; O(log n) to find it and O(n) in the members after it to close the gap |
| `pure func first(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the smallest member, null when empty; O(1) |
| `pure func last(self) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the largest member, null when empty; O(1) |
| `pure func get(self, index: Int) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the member at index in ascending order, null outside [0, count); O(1) |
| `pure func iterate(self) ListCursor[T] from self` | pure | the cursor of the sorted list, so a `for` visits the members from the smallest to the largest; O(1) to make, O(1) per step |
| `func each(self, visit: editable fn mut(T) Void)` | none | calls visit with a read loan of every member in ascending order; the callback may have effects, so `each` is not pure; O(n) plus the callback per member |
| `pure func fold[A](self, initial: owned A, step: pure fn(A, T) A) A` | pure | step gets a read loan of the accumulator and a member, once per member in ascending order, and returns the next accumulator; O(n) plus the callback per member |
| `pure func any(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for some member; stops at the first one that passes; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func all(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) Bool` | pure | whether holds is true for every member; stops at the first one that fails; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func find(self, holds: pure fn(T) Bool) (alias T from self)?` | pure | a read loan of the smallest member holds is true for, null when none does; O(n) plus the callback |
| `pure func toList(self) List[T] where T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a list of copies of the members in ascending order; allocates; O(n) |
| `pure func between(self, low: T, high: T) List[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | a list of copies of the members from low up to, but not including, high, in ascending order; empty when high is not above low; allocates; O(log n) to find low and O(k) for the k members copied |
| `pure func union(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the members of self and of other, each once, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m) |
| `pure func intersection(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the members both self and other hold, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m) |
| `pure func difference(self, other: SortedSet[T]) SortedSet[T] where T implements Comparable, T implements Copyable` | pure; alloc | copies of the members of self that other lacks, in ascending order; allocates; O(n + m) |

| `pure func sorted(items: ListView[Int]) List[Int]` | pure | Bottom-up merge sort: stable, O(n log n) comparisons and copies, O(n) extra space. |

### `class FileSystem implements Authority`

| Declaration | Effects | Contract |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted try func readText(self, path: Path) String` | alloc, fail, block, io | the UTF-8 contents of path below this root; fails `fs.outside_root` when the path is absolute or escapes the root, `fs.not_found`, `fs.not_a_file` or `fs.invalid_text`. Development adapter: the root is a fresh empty temporary directory per run, or FORTIS_DEV_ROOT when set; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func writeAll(self, path: Path, text: StringView)` | alloc, fail, block, io | replaces the contents of path with text, creating the file; fails `fs.outside_root` or `fs.not_found` (missing parent directory); blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
| `trusted try func readAll(self, path: Path) Bytes` | alloc, fail, block, io | the bytes of path; fails `fs.outside_root`, `fs.not_found` or `fs.not_a_file`; blocks the calling thread (the `block` effect, 11.1) |
